topic: Stripe + OpenRouter and the enterprise AI stack
angle: Multi-model gateways lower friction but shift lock-in up the stack—treat them like a core platform, not a shortcut.
sourceTitle: Stripe Acquiring OpenRouter, Aggregating AI?, Flipping the Business Model
linkedinPost:
The AI layer cake is reorganizing—are you ready for lock-in to move up the stack?

A recent analysis on Stratechery explores Stripe reportedly acquiring OpenRouter and the idea of “aggregating AI” behind a single gateway. Translation for enterprises: the multi-model switchboard is becoming a real platform, not a side utility.

From the trenches, gateways do two things well: they compress switching costs and standardize procurement. That’s gold when your product teams need to test models fast without renegotiating contracts.

But new convenience creates new dependencies. You can end up locked into the gateway’s roadmap, observability, pricing, and safety posture—while losing visibility into model-by-model performance.

My playbook: pilot via a gateway to learn quickly, but keep a direct path to critical models for your top-ROI use cases. Maintain a living model leaderboard per use case (quality, latency, cost, risk). Negotiate data controls, rate limits, egress fees, and exportable logs up front. And decide who owns the “last mile” prompts and evals—you, not the gateway.

If aggregation is the future, your leverage is the contract and your telemetry.

How are you balancing gateway speed with the risk of a new single point of failure? #AIStrategy #EnterpriseAI #AIAdoption #AITransformation
